guard: The three caller-authority stores are immutable at the broker: the admission and accepted stores are write-once per key, the evidence store is append-only and read first-on-key, and all three refuse rollup, message delete and purge. A key holder's own publish row cannot replace, widen, erase or empty what was recorded.
why: A run-admitter holds `$KV.cotal_admission_<s>.<its key>` and an issuer holds `$KV.cotal_issued_<s>.>`. A
publish row carries a Nats-Rollup header, a plain replacement, a deletion marker and a per-key purge,
and none of them is a CAS write, so the create-only CAS and the deletion-marker read see none of them.
Measured on a store built by the real provisioning path: `Nats-Rollup: sub` on the admitter's own key
replaced a `none` ceiling with `all` and dropped the revocation marker; `Nats-Rollup: all` on that one key
purged the other run's row. Each mutation removes one part of the shape; the suite reads the shape back
from the broker and exercises every route live, so the cell named is the one the broker stops refusing.
The ep-binding suite reads core through the binary's dist, so every mutation rebuilds core first.

mutations.name: the admission store keeps the three immutability flags but loses write-once (a plain second write lands)
mutations.expectRed: a plain second write onto an admission key is refused by the broker (write-once per key)
mutations.cell: a plain second write onto an admission key is refused by the broker (write-once per key)

mutations.name: the immutability flags are dropped from every authority store (rollup lands again)
mutations.find: export const AUTHORITY_STORE_IMMUTABLE_FLAGS = Object.freeze({ allow_rollup_hdrs: false, deny_delete: true, deny_purge: true });
mutations.expectRed: a `Nats-Rollup: sub` publish onto an admission key is refused by the broker
mutations.cell: a `Nats-Rollup: sub` publish onto an admission key is refused by the broker
